# mims-harvard/ToolUniverse — source dossier

**State:** M9 assessed, selected corrections released, pinned checkout removed. The distinct GWAS candidate remains open as M11-GWAS-07. No upstream setup script, agent workflow, dependency install, or ToolUniverse runtime was used.

## Pinned source and reuse boundary

- Upstream: [mims-harvard/ToolUniverse](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse), pinned at [`78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed`](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/commit/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed), dated 2026-09-24 17:06:39 UTC. The filtered, shallow local checkout at `references/work/tooluniverse/` is ignored and temporary; it has 8,698 tracked files at this revision.
- The pinned root [`LICENSE`](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/LICENSE) is Apache License 2.0. The pinned [documentation license page](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/docs/about/license.rst#L4-L15) instead says MIT and links an older TxAgent project. The actual root license governs this pinned source; the inconsistency rules out relying on the documentation page to clear reuse. [Optional PyMuPDF](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/pyproject.toml#L88-L94) is explicitly separated because it is AGPL/commercial. Other optional packages, hosted services, data, models, and individual connectors require their own terms check before reuse.
- The source's public README advertises a large scientific tool catalog, compact discovery mode, composition, and two-tier caching. Those are claims to inspect against shipped code and tests, not evidence of Google Co-Scientist behavior or proof of scientific validity.

## Source map and comparison

The library is a catalog and tool execution layer, not a complete hypothesis workflow. Its central [`ToolUniverse` runtime](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/execute_function.py#L336-L376) loads selected tools and dispatches sync/async invocations. Tool descriptions/configuration and separate `skills/` workflows are its prompt-facing surface; they do not replace our specialist prompts or graph.

| Concern | Shipped source and evidence | Comparison question |
|---|---|---|
| Discovery | [Registry](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/tool_registry.py#L58-L146) combines decorated/configured tools, a generated lazy map, AST fallback and plugin entry points. [Compact MCP mode](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/docs/guide/building_ai_scientists/compact_mode.rst#L6-L54) exposes list/grep/info/execute rather than sending the entire catalog to the model. | Does current tool selection already bound context, and would progressive disclosure improve a demonstrated lookup? |
| Finder | [Keyword discovery](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/tool_finder_keyword.py#L726-L791) uses TF-IDF; [embedding](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/tool_finder_embedding.py#L258-L280) and [LLM](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/tool_finder_llm.py#L442-L490) finders are separate optional paths. | Can deterministic discovery help without paid embeddings or an additional LLM route? |
| Parameter validation | [`BaseTool.validate_parameters`](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/base_tool.py#L340-L477) checks JSON Schema and gives unknown-key/typo guidance. | Does the existing MCP/engine boundary give equally actionable errors without revealing sensitive inputs? |
| Error envelope | [Error types](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/exceptions.py#L8-L36) carry class, retryability and suggested next steps; the [runtime envelope](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/execute_function.py#L4452-L4458) retains `status`, `error`, `error_details`. | Could a failure guide an agent's retry while preserving provenance and security? |
| Result cache | [Two-tier manager](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/cache/result_cache_manager.py#L47-L81) uses memory/SQLite, TTL, versioned namespace and singleflight; a [tool run opts in](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/execute_function.py#L2982-L3010). | Are current evidence retrieval caches provenance-safe, and is any added cache worth its invalidation cost? |
| Composition | [Compose functions](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/compose_tool.py#L18-L89) invoke other registered tools and auto-load regex-discovered dependencies; [degradation handling](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/compose_tool.py#L313-L333) can annotate missing dependencies. | Does our existing multi-source literature search need any of this, or would importing a second composition runtime bypass evidence and cost controls? |
| Connector adapters | [REST](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/base_rest_tool.py#L22), [GraphQL](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/graphql_tool.py#L128), and [MCP](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/mcp_client_tool.py#L275) sit beside provider-specific Python connectors and local-model configs. A [catalog-integrity test](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/tests/unit/test_compose_tool_dependencies.py#L58-L75) counts more than 1,000 names; that is catalog breadth, not 1,000 live-validated services. | Which individual connector fills a real scientific gap after checking our existing catalog, provider terms and live availability? |

The [tool-discovery agent configuration](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/data/tool_discovery_agents.json#L3-L47) supplies prompt-driven tool generation. It is not required to expose a selected connector through our existing MCP runtime. Inline [composition execution](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/compose_tool.py#L422-L450) invokes `exec` on configured code; importing it would add a separate trusted-code execution path outside the current confinement boundary, so this campaign will assess the composition idea without running or adopting that path.

## Tests and operational assumptions

[Upstream unit tests](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/tests/unit/test_cache_manager.py#L11-L47) exercise cache TTL and restart; [composition tests](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/tests/unit/test_compose_tool_dependencies.py#L58-L75) cover dependency declarations, and an [MCP integration suite](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/tests/integration/test_mcp_protocol.py) covers the protocol. The pinned [pytest configuration](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/pytest.ini#L1-L10) excludes network, API-key and slow tests by default, so shipped tests do not prove every connector works live or produces valid scientific evidence. None has been executed in this campaign checkout.

The [MCP server](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/smcp_server.py#L789-L794) defaults to loopback and requires a bearer-token environment variable for non-loopback binding. [Request-scoped credentials](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/docs/guide/api_keys.rst#L14-L53) are documented as cache-disabled and instance-partitioned. Calls can transmit arguments to [more than 200 providers](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/PRIVACY.md#L25-L35); some consume [account credits](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/data/api_keys_catalog.json#L293-L300), and the optional embedding finder downloads model weights. Their service/privacy terms and billing paths must be verified per selected connector. No upstream agent setup, broad install, ambient-key experiment or paid service is authorized.

## Current local counterpart

The current [`ToolRegistry`](../../engine/src/co_scientist/config/registry.py) merges default, user and custom YAML and reconciles disabled tools with their workflow search sources. [`tools.yaml`](../../engine/src/co_scientist/config/tools.yaml) already configures PubMed, OpenAlex, Europe PMC, arXiv, bioRxiv, web search and enrichment families including ChEMBL, UniProt, STRING, Reactome, Open Targets, Ensembl, gnomAD and clinical trials. The [MCP client](../../engine/src/co_scientist/mcp_client_session.py) discovers runtime-advertised schemas and filters the model-visible set by workflow whitelist; its [provider wrapper](../../engine/src/co_scientist/tools/provider.py) gives the model an error result for a bad individual call. [Literature search](../../engine/src/co_scientist/agents/generation/literature_review/search.py) queries enabled sources concurrently, deduplicates and budgets results. The [campaign tool gate](../../engine/mcp_server/campaign.py) withholds metered tools, and [research-call rows](../../app/app/store/schema_retrieval_calls.py) connect deep-research results to persisted evidence and report summaries. A ToolUniverse connector must pass through these existing seams; its registration alone would not give a run provenance or make a paid provider free.

## Fidelity boundary

Google's public product description calls for a grounded knowledge base whose ideas link to verified scientific references, and the paper describes literature-informed specialist agents ([local source extraction](../../docs/FIDELITY.md)). It does not prescribe ToolUniverse's catalog size, protocol, cache design or connector roster. Every ToolUniverse finding is therefore an **external technique** until separately justified by an observed local gap; connector choice and adapter shape are **local design choices**. A new tool must preserve our source IDs, claim/evidence lineage, safety gate and zero-cost routing rather than implying that its presence makes an idea scientifically validated.

## Candidate decisions

All entries below are **external techniques**; the connector roster and reuse routes are **local design choices**. No entry establishes a private Google implementation detail. A final disposition requires the stated boundary to be checked, not merely a matching name in either catalog.

| ID and concern | Upstream and local comparison | Boundary, result/cost and disposition |
|---|---|---|
| M9-DIS-01 — compact discovery | ToolUniverse's [compact list/grep/info/execute](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/docs/guide/building_ai_scientists/compact_mode.rst#L45-L54) is useful when its entire 1,000-name catalog would overflow a prompt. Our [MCP client](../../engine/src/co_scientist/mcp_client_session.py) discovers a much smaller manifest, then `get_tools(whitelist=...)` hands only each workflow's authorized subset to the model. | **Already covered** for the current engine tool workflow; a second finder or 1,000-tool surface has no demonstrated user gap. Test boundary: existing registry/MCP whitelist tests; no new inference, copy or dependency. Reopen only if a selected connector makes current context size material. |
| M9-ERR-02 — schema and recoverable errors | Upstream [JSON Schema validation](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/base_tool.py#L340-L477) and [structured errors](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/exceptions.py#L8-L36) give typo/retry hints. Our [MCP discovery](../../engine/src/co_scientist/mcp_client_session.py) converts advertised schemas, and [`MCPToolProvider.execute_tool_call`](../../engine/src/co_scientist/tools/provider.py) returns malformed arguments, unknown tools and tool failures as a tool-role error instead of aborting the whole loop. | **Already covered** for error containment and schema advertisement. A richer hint is not yet tied to a failed scientific workflow; no new envelope is justified. Existing tool-call tests are the boundary. No code, inference or cost. |
| M9-CACHE-03 — evidence on cached retrieval | Upstream's [versioned opt-in result cache](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/cache/result_cache_manager.py#L47-L81) prompted a local audit. Our [literature node](../../engine/src/co_scientist/agents/generation/literature_review/node.py) saved its result before appending `research_ledgers`, while cached articles retained a deep-research `retrieval_call_id`. The [app drain](../../app/app/engine_adapter/drain_research.py) writes call rows only from ledgers, but [evidence](../../app/app/engine_adapter/drain_hypotheses.py) retains the article call ID, so a cache hit could leave an orphaned provenance pointer and omit a report summary. Campaign-free/BYOK modes bypass this cache. | **Adopted independent local correctness fix.** A red persistent-cache test reproduced a researched article without its ledger. The node now stores its completed result; an old entry with researched article IDs but no ledger is treated as stale and refreshed. Engine tests verify no repeated search on a valid hit, legacy refresh, and unaffected ordinary/forced cache hits. An app integration test carries the actual cache result through drain and report: one matching retrieval row and data-source summary survive, while a Phase 2-only article gets no invented call ID. Local runs: 17 engine and 8 app tests passed; Ruff, format and diff checks passed. No upstream code/dependency, network or model cost. |
| M9-COMP-04 — tool composition | Upstream [compositions](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/compose_tool.py#L18-L89) resolve tool dependencies, while our [multi-source literature search](../../engine/src/co_scientist/agents/generation/literature_review/search.py) already runs configured sources concurrently, merges/deduplicates results and enforces a paper budget. Upstream [inline `exec`](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/compose_tool.py#L422-L450) would create a separate execution path. | **Already covered** for current literature composition; **rejected** inline `exec` because it would bypass the existing confinement/runtime boundary. Existing search and sandbox tests are the boundary; no code, inference or dependency. |
| M9-ERR-05 — failed biomedical lookup reads as no hit | Upstream's [REST adapter](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/base_rest_tool.py#L463-L490) distinguishes request failures from valid responses. Our [`search_chembl`/`search_uniprot`](../../engine/mcp_server/tools/biomedical_databases.py) previously returned `{source, query, records: []}` both for zero hits and for HTTP/parse failures. | **Adopted independent local correction.** A red registered FastMCP test reproduced the ambiguity. The two tools now keep their success/zero-hit envelope and add non-secret `error.kind` on HTTP, malformed, missing-field, network and timeout failures; a failed provider stays non-fatal. Eight focused MCP tests, Ruff and format checks pass. One keyless live response from each public API returned a record (`CHEMBL25` for aspirin; a UniProt accession for the broad EGFR query), showing the real endpoint path still works; no scientific claim follows from the hit. No retry, new dependency, model inference or paid service. |
| M9-RET-06 — retraction status | ToolUniverse ships a [DOI-based Crossref checker](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/retraction_tool.py#L47-L130), but our [`citation_resolver`](../../app/app/citation_resolver.py) already checks every DOI against a committed [Crossref/Retraction Watch extract](../../app/app/retraction_set.py), persists `evidence.retracted`, and labels it in the [report bibliography](../../app/app/report_markdown_bibliography.py) and Learning tab. A live keyless Crossref response verified two retraction notices; its original DOI `10.1021/am300292v` was already in the local set. The dataset refresh added 1,331 DOI entries and removed 2, with `10.1002/1873-3468.13480` newly recognized by the production resolver path. [Evidence](tooluniverse/m9-retraction-refresh.json) retains source, hashes, counts, checks and costs. | **Adopted existing-data refresh; separate live connector already covered for this workflow.** The 37 targeted resolver/report tests passed; the real newly added DOI resolved as `retracted` without a model call. No absence-of-notice result is labeled clean. The current report shows the positive status but not notice DOI/type; an additional per-DOI network lookup would add provider traffic without a demonstrated reader requirement. Existing dataset attribution remains in `NOTICE`. No upstream code or dependency was copied. |
| M9-GWAS-07 — curated association lookup | Upstream's [GWAS Catalog v2 adapter](https://github.com/mims-harvard/ToolUniverse/blob/78883724c46a94ec1d1bfdc984efb25ba1b76aed/src/tooluniverse/gwas_tool.py#L555-L607) exposes association ID, p-value/effect size, trait ontology and study accession. Current [Open Targets tools](../../engine/src/co_scientist/config/tools.yaml) cover target/disease association but not human SNP-level GWAS results. The [official v2 API](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/docs/programmatic-access/rest-api/) has a 15-query/second public limit and pagination; the upstream transport makes one 60-second request without a rate limiter. The official [rs334 training example](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/online/courses/human-genetic-variation-exploring-publicly-available-data/cast-study-2-search-for-a-variant-rs334/exploring-phenotypes-associated-with-a-variant/) shows distinct SNP/trait evidence, but does not validate the live API. | **Promising; final selection transferred open to M11-GWAS-07.** One bounded keyless `rs334` association request timed out after 20 seconds with zero bytes; one different documented SNP-by-ID path returned HTTP 500 (`timestamp`, `status`, `error`, `path`), not an association. The official [FAQ](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/docs/faq/) describes curated top associations, service/data terms and that its p-value inclusion threshold is not proof of genome-wide significance; neither association nor mapped gene is causal evidence. A real response, study context, access date, terms and bounded pagination/error/provenance behavior are prerequisites for integration. No unverified connector, broad dependency, model inference or metered service was added. |

Source exclusions: OpenAlex duplicates the current default connector, so its ToolUniverse adapter is **already covered**; AlphaFold structure lookup is deliberately absent from our qualitative-fidelity workflow, so adding it by catalog presence alone is **outside this campaign's authorized scope**. Neither exclusion asserts the source's live availability or scientific validity.

## M11 GWAS availability follow-up

The previously failing official v2 endpoint returned a [keyless `rs334` association response](tooluniverse/m11-gwas-live-response.json) on 24 September 2026 (HTTP 200 in 1.13 seconds, page 0 of 134 at size 1). The retained response identifies study `GCST90480652`, PubMed `39024449`, the reported platelet-count trait, p-value and beta context, and a next-page link. This is a live service-availability result, not yet evidence that a local connector works. The official [v2 reference](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/rest/api/v2/docs) documents pagination and a 15-query-per-second limit; the [GWAS Catalog FAQ](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/docs/faq/) places non-summary-statistics Catalog data under EBI Services Terms of Use. M11-GWAS-07 remains open for a bounded, provenance-preserving MCP integration and real tool-level check. An association or mapped gene is not a causal finding.

## Release evidence

M9-CACHE-03 and M9-ERR-05 have local code changes and bounded tests; M9-RET-06 refreshed the existing retraction extract. The [24 September official OpenRouter catalog receipt](tooluniverse/m9-free-route-2026-09-24.json) shows the selected Nex Pro route at zero prompt/completion price through its advertised 25 September date. A non-secret Railway production readback found `MODEL_NAME`, `SUPERVISOR_MODEL_NAME`, `CHAT_MODEL_NAME` and `SEMANTIC_SAFETY_MODEL` all set to that exact route; `CLAIM_VERIFIER_MODEL` remains unset and inherits the main model. The request boundary rechecks price/date and binds zero-price caps. No model inference was used for source assessment or local verification; the single bounded production browser probe is described below. M10-OPS-01 retains a hard prerequisite for any inference after expiry.

The final local branch at `537f0861` passed `make test-all` (3,151 engine, 1,986 app, 296 MCP, 115-row parity and its own tests), `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make build`, `make eval-smoke`, all 784 frontend tests, and 16/16 browser E2E cases on isolated ports 8118/5283. The default E2E port 8108 was held by a separate server from the original checkout and was left untouched. One full-browser attempt timed out waiting for an offline run to publish; that case passed alone and the next full run passed 16/16 without a code or threshold change. The repository's 500-line file and 40-code-line function gates were repaired after their initial red checks, not waived. An independent Luna 6/xhigh review found only an old extract date in `NOTICE`, which was corrected; no other correctness, security, cost or attribution finding remained. Scoped cleanup removed test-only dependency symlinks; Ruff F401/F841 and diff checks found no dead imports, variables or whitespace defects. Generated ignored build/Playwright outputs stay local to the isolated worktree and are not runtime dependencies.

The code-bearing [PR #37](https://github.com/guy915/Co-Scientist/pull/37) merged as `bbeda0c8b596ef2d0e9e958c48409bade37b362c`. Its GitHub Actions workflow failed before the first runner step, with dependent jobs skipped; the user explicitly waived hosted CI after the required local suite passed and the 15-file PR diff was reviewed. Railway API deployment `9b56d9dc-bd35-4887-b248-05b165e7c6b0` and MCP deployment `857769d8-b907-4d42-b770-64cca378cef9` reached SUCCESS on the merge commit; Vercel production deployment `dpl_79t1iGsqHvyhuZ36fBrZq1bUk82H` reached READY on the same commit. The API kept one replica, its `/app/data` volume, `RAILWAY_RUN_UID=0`, `/tmp/coscientist-cache`, and the exact Nex Pro free route in all four named model roles. The existing production smoke evaluator passed all five checks after both Railway services became healthy. In the deployed MCP image, a bounded keyless call to the changed ChEMBL function returned one aspirin record and a call to the changed UniProt function returned one EGFR result, each with no error. No migration or configuration change was required.

A fresh official OpenRouter catalog query immediately before the bounded browser probe still showed `nex-agi/nex-n2.5-pro:free` with zero prompt/completion price and advertised 25 September expiry. The campaign-owned public EGFR goal entered the production browser interview, but the model streamed prolonged reasoning without a final interview answer. The probe was stopped before creating a DRAFT or starting a research run. Its exact served model and request token cost were not independently observed; the configured route and public price alone do not prove those facts. This is a capability limit for M10-OPS-01, not scientific-quality evidence or a completed end-to-end run. No repeated model trial followed. The clean pinned ToolUniverse checkout was moved out of `references/work/` after release verification; no runtime depends on it. The per-component attribution remains in this dossier and `NOTICE`, while M11-GWAS-07 retains the promising unresolved connector.
